A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SensorLLM work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the revised title and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original sensor-description evaluations, human assessments, HAR results across five datasets, and ablation and cross-dataset experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and additionally reports classification accuracy and a special-token ablation.

M1.justification: The frozen Chronos and LLM backbones, alignment MLP, channel tokens, two training stages, input construction, and losses remain unchanged. SENSORQA names the existing generated training material; the token-removal experiment evaluates an ablated variant rather than revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use USC-HAD, UCI-HAR, PAMAP2, MHealth, and CAPTURE-24 for the same description and classification tasks. SENSORQA packages the existing coverage, and the new token ablation uses retained datasets and channel configurations. No zero-shot evaluation is added.

E2.justification: GPT-4o remains the description-generation comparator, and Table 2 retains the same eleven HAR baselines, including Chronos+MLP, GPT4TS, and Attend. Existing Task-only and model-size comparisons are also retained; baseline descriptions move from Appendix A.7 to A.8.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds accuracy alongside macro-F1. The new special-token experiment compares token inclusion and removal using the two-layer alignment MLP specified in Table 4. Existing splits, windowing, preprocessing, training budgets, and human-evaluation sampling remain unchanged; newly reported dataset counts are disclosure rather than demonstrated sample-size changes.

E4.justification: v3 adds a targeted ablation of channel-boundary special tokens on MHealth and PAMAP2 in Section 5 and Table 4. The alignment, prompt, MLP-depth, model-size, cross-dataset, and appendix qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 4 supplies uncertainty for deeper-MLP results previously shown only as averages in v2 Figure 3: MHealth 90.2±3.11 and PAMAP2 85.8±0.84. The stated five-trial mean-and-standard-deviation protocol otherwise remains unchanged; no increase in repetitions or new significance test is documented.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds accuracy scores for all twelve models across five datasets while preserving every original macro-F1 entry. The new ablation reports 89.6 versus 90.2 on MHealth and 84.4 versus 85.8 on PAMAP2, without versus with special tokens. Description scores, existing ablation plots, cross-dataset results, and qualitative outputs remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 retain the same alignment mapping, objectives, input construction, Chronos tokenization, and macro-F1 definitions. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, first contribution, and conclusion newly present release of the named SENSORQA dataset as a contribution, replacing the earlier emphasis on the automatic generation approach and its pipeline. The central two-stage framework, competitive five-dataset performance, and cross-dataset alignment claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation that special tokens preserve channel structure and reduce modality confusion, and recommends a single hidden layer as an accuracy–efficiency compromise. Section 7 newly attributes omitted zero-shot evaluation to unavailable comparable baselines, while ambiguously suggesting unseen-class generalization despite reporting no such experiment.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.7 and Table 12 document SENSORQA's organization and train/test sample counts for both stages across all five datasets. v3 states release of the dataset, whereas v2 states release of code and the generation pipeline. Existing templates, hardware, and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 removes Tan et al. (2024) and the introduction's claim to address that work's concerns about LLMs for time series. It adds positioning around prior approaches' variable-input limitations and the claimed absence of comparable zero-shot methods. Section 2 and Appendix A.1 otherwise retain their research coverage.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method exposition, results discussion, ablation narrative, and conclusion around SENSORQA and multivariate alignment. It changes the title and several subsection headings, removes duplicated introductory wording, and inserts a dedicated dataset appendix. This is broad narrative revision despite stable underlying methods.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains input-type labels and revised sensor illustrations; Figure 2 adds backward arrows and a direction legend. Table 2 gains accuracy columns, new Tables 4 and 12 present the token ablation and sample counts, and the cross-dataset table redisplays existing same-dataset controls. Other changes mainly involve captions, relocation, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves empirical support and transparency through the targeted special-token ablation, complementary accuracy results, and explicit dataset sample counts. These strengthen documentation of the existing work without changing its principal findings. The new, ambiguous unseen-class generalization wording in Section 7 weakens claim calibration, but the added evidence and documentation still provide a limited net improvement.
